item.title: UK’s East Midlands region invests in 189 electric buses
item.dc:creator: guest author
item.description: The UK's East Midlands region has been granted a £47.55 million investment for 189 battery-electric buses to replace older diesel vehicles. The region's Mayor is driving the government investment with further proposed contributions from Arriva, Stagecoach, Nottingham City Transport, and Trentbarton, with four schemes worth more than £100m in total.

item.title: Why China’s electric cars are parking back and forth
item.dc:creator: Jasmin Apitzsch-Krause
item.description: In Chinese parking garages, electric cars have recently been seen parking and unparking themselves hundreds of times. Behind this curious phenomenon is apparently a competition by tech giant Huawei with some absurd consequences.

media:content.media:title: Why China’s electric cars are parking back and forth - electrive.com
media:content.media:description: Auf YouTube findest du die angesagtesten Videos und Tracks. Außerdem kannst du eigene Inhalte hochladen und mit Freunden oder gleich der ganzen Welt teilen.

item.title: Hyundai launches Neira three-row EV in Indonesia
item.dc:creator: Sagar Parikh
item.description: Three months after showcasing the Neira as a near-production prototype at GIIAS 2026, Hyundai has launched its final version at Gaikindo AutoWeek (GAW) 2026. The Neira is the company's first locally produced seven-seat EV in the country.

item.title: BYD starts deploying Flash Chargers in Malaysia
item.dc:creator: Sagar Parikh
item.description: BYD has deployed its first Flash Chargers in Malaysia, coinciding with the launch of the new Denza D9 featuring the second-generation Blade battery that can take advantage of the latest infrastructure. Access to these megawatt chargers will soon be offered to all EV brands.

item.title: New graphite could enable faster charging
item.dc:creator: Jasmin Apitzsch-Krause
item.description: Researchers at Rice University in the US have developed a process that can produce synthetic graphite for fast-charging lithium-ion batteries in just 0.2 seconds. At the same time, the process could significantly reduce the synthetic graphite production energy usage and production costs of the anode material.

item.title: Suzuki Ignis Electric celebrates world premiere
item.dc:creator: Victoria Zippmann
item.description: Suzuki's new electric microcar is celebrating its world premiere. With it, the Suzuki Ignis name also returns to Europe. On the German market, the car will become the smallest fully-fledged electric car at 3.57 meters long.

item.title: Karsan to build 35 trolleybuses for Bologna
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: Turkish manufacturer Karsan has won a tender from TPER, the public transport operator of Bologna, Italy. The contract initially covers 35 units of Karsan's new 18-meter-long e-ATA trolleybus, with a contractual option for 35 additional units.

item.title: General Motors to transition to native NACS charging ports in South Korea
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: General Motors has signed an agreement in South Korea to adopt the North American Charging Standard (NACS) with Tesla. The deal extends an existing NACS agreement, which GM originally signed in 2023 for North America, to the Korean market.

item.title: Tata Group’s British battery cell factory faces delays
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: There appear to be difficulties in the construction of the Tata Group's British battery cell factory in Somerset. According to media reports, a second construction contractor has already dropped out within five months. It remains uncertain whether the planned completion next year can be achieved as scheduled.

item.title: Electric Porsche 718 Boxster heads for series production
item.dc:creator: Victoria Zippmann
item.description: The all-electric Porsche 718 Boxster is on the verge of series production, according to its German carmaker. It is set to become the most powerful 718 to date and will come standard with a switchable virtual transmission and a six-cylinder boxer engine sound. The electric Boxster is expected to make its world premiere in the first quarter of 2027.

item.title: Iveco Bus introduces new battery generation
item.dc:creator: Jasmin Apitzsch-Krause
item.description: Iveco Bus is introducing a new generation of NMC batteries for its electric city and intercity buses. Depending on the model and configuration, these enable up to 100 kilometers of additional range. The manufacturer is also offering an optional battery warranty of up to 15 years.

item.title: British EVs could soon qualify as ‘Made in Europe’
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: According to EU diplomats, EU member states are inclined to integrate British electric vehicles under "Made in Europe" guidelines. The European Union could apply similar credentials to the other states of the European Economic Area such as Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, and Switzerland.

item.title: BYD to acquire former Smart factory in Hambach
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: BYD is negotiating with Ineos Automotive to purchase its plant in Hambach, France, as both companies have now officially announced. The fact that both parties are reporting on the transaction before finalizing the deal indicates the advanced stage of the negotiations.

item.title: Chery Group starts assembling Lepas EVs in Thailand
item.dc:creator: Sagar Parikh
item.description: Chinese conglomerate Chery Group has started assembling electric cars of its newest brand in Thailand, Lepas, beginning with the L6 EV. The company has an ICE L6 and a L6 PHEV also in its global line-up, but in Thailand, it produces and sells only the L6 EV.

item.title: VW and Elli launch €1,995 V2G BiDi wallbox
item.dc:creator: Victoria Zippmann
item.description: Volkswagen and its energy subsidiary Elli will introduce their first Vehicle-to-Grid package to the German market in December 2026. The requisite DC wallbox will cost €1,995 euros. In addition to VW, VW Commercial Vehicles, and Cupra, Skoda will also be included in the launch. Details about the electricity tariff have also been announced.

item.title: Switzerland: VMCV orders up to 47 Yutong electric buses
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: Swiss public transport operator VMCV has signed a framework agreement with Yutong for the delivery of up to 47 electric buses. The Chinese brand won the tender against three competitors. The contract is worth around 30 million francs, equivalent to just under €33 million euros.

item.title: Exicom to sell DC fast charger manufacturer Tritium
item.dc:creator: Jasmin Apitzsch-Krause
item.description: Just under two years after acquiring the insolvent Australian fast charger manufacturer Tritium, Indian charging infrastructure provider Exicom is looking to divest the company once again. A non-binding agreement values the company at US$85 million.

item.title: Switzerland: Fastned, Obornes and Milence secure initial truck charging network
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: The Swiss Federal Roads Office (FEDRO) has awarded the 32 locations tendered in January 2026 for the construction of a total of 82 truck charging stations along national roads to three companies. Lot 1 goes to Fastned, Lot 2 to Obornes, and Lot 3 to Milence.

item.title: New battery generation from Forsee Power: ZEN 8 now with 173 Ah LFP cells
item.dc:creator: Victoria Zippmann
item.description: Forsee Power introduces the ZEN 8 LFP for light construction, agricultural, and municipal vehicles. The battery uses the same dimensions and mounting points as the ZEN 8 NMC, enabling deployment without changes to the vehicle design.

item.title: Infineon introduces power module for commercial electric vehicles
item.dc:creator: Jasmin Apitzsch-Krause
item.description: Semiconductor manufacturer Infineon is expanding its portfolio with a power module for traction inverters in electric commercial vehicles. The new HybridPACK HD is based on silicon carbide technology and is designed for a service life of more than 1.2 million kilometers.

item.title: Fortum tests new battery recycling process
item.dc:creator: Jasmin Apitzsch-Krause
item.description: For the first time, Fortum Battery Recycling has produced customer samples of nickel sulfate, cobalt sulfate, and lithium hydroxide in battery grade using its new recycling process. The materials, obtained at the Harjavalta facility in Finland, are currently being evaluated by potential customers.

item.title: BASF supplies CATL: CAM shipments from Schwarzheide have begun
item.dc:creator: Victoria Zippmann
item.description: BASF has begun deliveries to CATL. The supply contract includes the provision of high-performance cathode materials from BASF's plant in Schwarzheide (Germany). CATL also receives battery materials from BASF in China.

item.title: EU introduces import quotas for hybrids from China and other countries
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: It's official - from December, the European Union will introduce import quotas for hybrid cars from China, as well as restrict imports from other countries. The regulation will initially apply for 200 days, limiting the import of hybrid cars from China to exactly 191,780 units during this period.

item.title: Škoda Group restructures its rail, bus and drivetrain businesses
item.dc:creator: Victoria Zippmann
item.description: Škoda Group is reorganising its business to improve efficiency and place greater emphasis on its products and services. As part of the changes, Škoda Vagonka will be integrated into existing subsidiary Škoda Transportation, while Škoda Electric will be split into two joint-stock companies. Further changes are planned for 2027.

item.title: No more factory teams: Stellantis exits motorsport
item.dc:creator: Victoria Zippmann
item.description: Stellantis has exited the WEC and bid farewell to Formula E. This marks a radical shift for the group's motorsport strategy, especially considering Opel's newly developed Gen4 race car and the group's original commitment until 2030. Citroën must also say goodbye to Formula E, and in the WEC, Peugeot's recently updated 9X8 will not race. Here's how Stellantis plans to move forward.

item.title: ACEA: battery-electric cars capture 30 per cent of EU passenger car market
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: In the EU, more than 250,000 pure electric cars are now hitting the roads each month. In October, this figure reached 280,000 units, a substantial increase of 61 per cent year-on-year. Across the EU's overall passenger car market, the share of EVs climbed to nearly 30 per cent.

item.title: VW starts production of the long wheelbase ID. Buzz Cargo
item.dc:creator: Jasmin Apitzsch-Krause
item.description: Volkswagen Commercial Vehicles has started series production of the long wheelbase ID. Buzz Cargo at its main Hanover plant. The long version of the electric transporter, which has been available to order since September, offers 4.4 cubic meters of cargo volume, an 86-kWh battery, and a range of up to 490 km.

item.title: ‘The big advantage for us lies in flexibility’ – Electra manager Paul Tonini on battery storage
item.dc:creator: Florian Treiss
item.description: Electra is increasingly relying on battery storage systems for its fast-charging parks. In Germany alone, 20 storage systems are already installed, and this number is expected to reach around 40 by the end of the year. In this interview, Germany CEO Paul Tonini explains the advantages of the technology, why grid operators sometimes complicate its deployment, and why battery storage alone cannot solve the challenges of expanding the charging network.

item.title: Fraunhofer explores lighter fuel cell bipolar plates
item.dc:creator: Jasmin Apitzsch-Krause
item.description: The Fraunhofer Institute for Machine Tools and Forming Technology (IWU) has developed new manufacturing processes for particularly lightweight bipolar plates made of carbon fiber-reinforced plastic. The technology could make fuel cells for drones, small aircraft, and helicopters lighter and more compact in the future.

item.title: Mercedes receives KBA approval for door-to-door driving assistant
item.dc:creator: Florian Treiss
item.description: Mercedes-Benz has become the first automaker in Germany to receive regulatory approval for a point-to-point driving assistant. The German Federal Motor Transport Authority (KBA) approved the MB.Drive Assist Pro system based on UN Regulation R171. This enables automated door-to-door driving at SAE Level 2, including complex urban traffic situations.
